rules.sentence: One must consider the likelihood of airway abnormalities in patients with congenital heart disease, especially premature and with a weight of fewer than 10 kilograms.[10]
For example, patients with Trisomy 21 have a 50% incidence of congenital heart defects, so physical examination is crucial in defining these defects.[11]
A child presenting with congestive cardiac failure may have iron deficiency anemia.
A cyanotic patient may have erythrocytosis due to the blood's degree of desaturated hemoglobin.
A high hematocrit level requires an exchange transfusion before surgery to prevent neurological sequelae associated with excessive blood viscosity.
One may find prolongation of prothrombin time (PT) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) in cyanosis.
